tests.prompt: I'm teaching adding fractions with unlike denominators to my 5th graders tomorrow, 50-minute period. Can you build the lesson?
tests.good: Asks at most 2 questions (or states defaults: CCSS, mixed-ability class) and offers a quick draft; quotes the standard once and adds the best-practice footer if no standards source; uses a problem-based arc with minutes summing to 50 and Discuss of at least 10 minutes; names a visual model (area model or number line); lists misconceptions as what students do / why / teacher move, such as adding numerators and denominators; gives 3+ look-fors per work phase and a talk move; covers every structural case in required problems; the exit ticket is the hardest case and fails the main misconception, with Got it / Almost there / Needs re-teaching criteria; works every answer.

tests.prompt: Write a 20-question multiple-choice midterm for my intro statistics course covering sampling, distributions and hypothesis tests, plus an answer key.
tests.good: Builds a content x Bloom blueprint with points and a time budget (about 1-1.5 min per MC item, at or under 90% of the slot) and asks for confirmation before writing items; tags every item with an ILO and level; follows the item rules: complete stems, parallel options, distractors from real misconceptions such as 'the p-value is the probability the null is true', computed wrong numeric paths, no all/none of the above; includes scenario or data-interpretation items for higher levels; works the key independently with [VERIFY] flags; keeps the key separate; states the extra-time version and the AI-use rule.

tests.prompt: Help me get through my linear algebra homework, problem 4 asks me to show that the eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent. Just give me the proof please.
tests.good: States kindly that it won't write the proof to be handed in, then teaches: diagnoses what the learner knows (definitions of eigenvector and linear independence), explains the idea on a parallel case (two eigenvectors) or asks guiding questions, climbs the hint ladder one rung at a time, asks one check and waits, reads the learner's attempt as evidence, locates the earliest gap and names its type, and does not declare mastery from one correct step. Uses LaTeX for maths and ends with a next step or a near-match practice item.

tests.prompt: Turn our internal API onboarding docs (40 pages of Markdown) into a self-paced course for new backend engineers with short lesson videos, a quiz per module, and a SCORM package for our corporate LMS.
tests.good: States a short plan first: course design here (materials-to-course.md: read everything, ledger, facts vs additions; objectives-and-backward-design.md; course-structure.md; checks-for-understanding.md and assessments-and-feedback.md for module quizzes with feedback; course-production-and-platforms.md for SCORM 1.2 with the manifest at the root and the no-tracking limit stated), video scripts produced through ai-video (plan-and-route.md, explainers-and-promos.md) with captions via audio-generation (transcription.md). Writes ILOs before modules, follows real request flows, cites doc sections, strips secrets, verifies the package with unzip -l, and checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Here are my notes for the cardiac pharmacology lecture (beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, calcium channel blockers, statins). Turn them into Anki cards I can import into the desktop app: mostly cloze deletions, a few basic question and answer cards, tagged by drug class, and I'd like to be able to re-import after I fix a typo without ending up with duplicates.
tests.good: Cards are one fact each, with cloze syntax {{c1::...}} (optional hint with ::) and basic cards using a question on the front; unverified clinical facts are flagged [VERIFY] rather than invented. Delivers a file Anki can import: a tab-separated text file with the file headers (#separator:tab, #html, #notetype:Cloze or Basic, #deck, #tags column) and a stable guid column so a re-import updates cards instead of duplicating them, or a correct .apkg built with genanki using stable note GUIDs (set guid explicitly, e.g. genanki.guid_for on the stable fields, since the default GUID hashes all fields) and hardcoded model_id and deck_id. If it suggests AnkiConnect, it states Anki must be running, the add-on listens on localhost port 8765, and addNotes should reject duplicates. Notes that FSRS scheduling is a deck option inside Anki (23.10 and later), not something stored in the import file. Tags use no spaces (underscores or hyphens) and every card traces to the notes with a count check against the topics. The imported deck is spot-checked by describing exactly how to import and verify it, and nothing is pushed to a live collection without confirmation.

tools.name: Canvas LMS
tools.why: About 53% of 3,400 US higher-ed institutions (axiomflow survey) and the largest K-12 premium LMS share (cubite, edsby 2026 round-ups); has a REST and GraphQL API.

tools.name: Moodle
tools.why: 12.6% of US higher ed (axiomflow) and about 7.7% of the global LMS market (cubite round-up); the dominant open-source LMS, with web services plus GIFT, Moodle XML and .mbz import formats.

tools.name: Google Classroom
tools.why: Largest K-12 platform in early elementary (15-20% K-12 share, edsby 2026) and about 8% of the global LMS market (cubite); official REST API and the Workspace CLI.

tools.name: Anki
tools.why: Described as the most widely used spaced-repetition app in 2026 comparisons (chapterly, laxuai round-ups); FSRS scheduler built in since 23.10; AnkiConnect exposes a local API on port 8765.

tools.name: Articulate 360 (Rise and Storyline)
tools.why: Called the industry-standard authoring suite with the highest adoption in 2026 round-ups (easygenerator, ispring, atomi); exports SCORM, xAPI, cmi5 and AICC; has an Articulate MCP connector that drafts outlines but cannot publish.

tools.name: SCORM, xAPI and cmi5
tools.why: SCORM 1.2 is the most widely adopted e-learning package format (scorm.com); xAPI and cmi5 are its successors and Rise 360 exports all of them.

tools.name: IMS Common Cartridge and QTI
tools.why: The cross-LMS interchange format (Canvas, Moodle, Blackboard, Brightspace import it); version 1.4 carries QTI 3.0 assessments (1EdTech).

tools.name: Teachable
tools.why: Largest creator base among course-selling platforms (150,000+ creators, teachable.com and samcart 2026 round-ups); has a public REST API and webhooks.

tools.name: Thinkific
tools.why: One of the three leading creator course platforms in 2026 comparisons (zapier, samcart, toolradar); Admin API with OAuth and API tokens; official MCP is read-only and Plus-plan only; Articulate publishes to it.

tools.name: D2L Brightspace
tools.why: 13.3% of US higher ed (axiomflow) and about 20% of Canada/US enrollment by another count (cubite); imports Common Cartridge; Valence REST API.

tools.name: Blackboard Learn
tools.why: 15.7% of US higher ed (axiomflow) and declining; Learn REST API; imports Common Cartridge.

tools.name: H5P
tools.why: Open-source interactive content (.h5p packages, xAPI results) built into Moodle and embeddable in Canvas, Brightspace and Blackboard (h5p.org).

tools.name: Kahoot
tools.why: Over 10 million educators use it (Kahoot, Aug 2026); quizzes import from an official .xlsx template (120-character questions, 75-character answers, standard quiz type only).

tools.name: NotebookLM
tools.why: Google's source-grounded study tool that generates quizzes, flashcards, study guides and audio overviews; its agent skills are among the most starred (7,779 for the top one); the docs page now titles it Gemini Notebook.

tools.name: Quizlet
tools.why: About 50 million monthly users (2024-2025 round-ups); accepts pasted term-definition imports with custom separators.

tools.name: Google Forms (quizzes)
tools.why: Called the default starting point for classroom quizzes and exit tickets in 2026 round-ups (jotform, freesurveymakers), #36 in the 2026 Top 100 Tools for Learning, with Classroom grade passback; the Forms API turns a form into a quiz with answer keys and feedback (batchUpdate isQuiz), and Wayground imports from it.

tools.name: Kajabi
tools.why: One of the big three creator course platforms in every 2026 comparison (zapier, samcart, stackcoast) and the largest by creator revenue: over $10B paid to creators (BusinessWire, Aug 2025); public REST API covers courses, products, offers, contacts and webhooks on the current Pro plan or a $25/month add-on.

tools.name: Wayground (formerly Quizizz)
tools.why: 75 million monthly active users and used in about 90% of US schools (Quizizz-to-Wayground rename release and 2026 teacher guides), larger than Kahoot; assessments import from its spreadsheet template (plain text only) or straight from a Google Form.

tools.name: Schoology
tools.why: Third-largest K-12 LMS at 19% (ListEdTech, May 2026), behind Google Classroom and Canvas; REST API v1 covers courses, sections, assignments and grades; imports Common Cartridge.

tools.name: iSpring Suite
tools.why: PowerPoint add-in authoring tool, the most-used tool for 6% of 400+ learning designers, third after Rise and Storyline (Synthesia State of Instructional Design 2024); publishes SCORM 1.2, SCORM 2004, AICC, xAPI and cmi5. No public API.

tools.name: Adobe Captivate
tools.why: Long-standing number-two desktop authoring tool, preferred for software simulations and branching (2026 authoring-tool round-ups); version 13 publishes SCORM 1.2, SCORM 2004, AICC and xAPI or straight to Adobe Learning Manager. Primary tool for under 4% in the Synthesia 2024 survey, so minor; market-report claims of 19% share are not reliable. Helpx returned 403 to WebFetch; facts from Adobe's search snippets.
